title: The teacher, the copy, and the community
summary: An introduction to the stronger earlier-Teacher reconstruction and the different things that could survive through transmission.
voice: First-person authorial script with a stock synthetic narrator; not an imitation of the author's voice.

scenes.title: More than a resemblance
scenes.narration: The stronger Teacher-transmission conjecture is not merely that Jesus resembled an earlier Jewish teacher. I ask whether an earlier founder's teachings, community and biography survived through successors, with the founding story later located in the familiar Jesus chronology.

scenes.title: Different histories can separate
scenes.narration: A teacher's lifetime, the first collection of sayings, a later literary arrangement, and a surviving manuscript are different historical questions. A date attached to one of them does not automatically answer all the others.

scenes.title: The objection must meet the actual theory
scenes.narration: A reply that assumes the same disciples had to live for more than a century misses the succession mechanism. The harder question is what could document successors, repeated names, inherited offices or changes in the presentation of relationships.

scenes.title: A concrete history of survival
scenes.narration: The Damascus Document provides a useful comparison. Copies from the Cairo Genizah and older witnesses from the Dead Sea Scrolls allow a work's survival to be examined across a large interval. A late copy need not mean a recently created work.

scenes.title: A precedent is not an identification
scenes.narration: That comparison opens a question about earlier layers in Thomas; it does not identify their author by itself. Distinctive readings, a traceable sayings collection, or a particular pattern of interpretation would do more work than a generic resemblance.

scenes.title: Texts and institutions need different links
scenes.narration: The institutional reconstruction also proposes relationships between communities in Judea and Egypt. Replacing that proposal with shared themes changes the claim. The question needs evidence about people, leadership, practices and places as well as books.

scenes.title: What does authority inherit?
scenes.narration: The Melchizedek investigation adds another dimension. A tradition can change the grounds of priestly legitimacy while preserving a recognizable figure or function. An inherited name, a family line, and an office must therefore be compared rather than treated as interchangeable.

scenes.title: Inspect the reconstruction
scenes.narration: The wiki keeps the stronger earlier-founder hypothesis, its revisions, and its objections available together. This episode is a doorway into that argument. The source atlas makes the works, copies, translations, and proposed historical links separately inspectable.
